name: dsh-doublecheck
hypothesis: Forces a requirements grill and red/green test evidence before the agent can claim a fix.
whyForSweBench: Lite tasks fail when a cheap model edits blindly. A test gate should raise resolve rate even if it costs tokens.

name: dsh-proof
hypothesis: Spawns a read-only verifier before the turn closes and steers gaps back into the loop.
whyForSweBench: SWE-bench scoring is exactly 'do hidden tests pass'. An independent check is the closest plugin-shaped proxy.

name: dsh-inspect
hypothesis: Adversarial checkup → fix → review loop.
whyForSweBench: Cheap models stop at the first plausible patch. An inspect loop should catch obvious regressions.

name: dsh-fail-logger
hypothesis: Dedupes failed tool calls into a skill so the agent stops repeating the same broken command.
whyForSweBench: Flash-class models loop on the same pytest invocation. A failure notebook is cheap intelligence.

name: dsh-pain-point-check
hypothesis: After two non-converged experiments, force the model to answer what actually failed before more edits.
whyForSweBench: Stops thrashing on the wrong file — a common Lite failure mode.

name: dsh-specflow
hypothesis: Turns the issue into a spec + goal-backed tasks before implementation.
whyForSweBench: Lite problem statements are real GitHub issues. A spec layer should keep the cheap model on the reported symptom.

name: dsh-plannotator
hypothesis: Anchored plan review before the agent spends the edit budget.
whyForSweBench: Useful if the plan stays short. Harmful if it burns the cheap model's context on ceremony.

name: dsh-task-planner
hypothesis: Condition-reflex planning: recall similar past tasks, then decompose against current tools.
whyForSweBench: Cross-instance memory of 'how I fixed django queryset bugs' could transfer inside a Lite run.

name: dsh-track
hypothesis: Decision-point protocol and a Linear-style issue store inside the session.
whyForSweBench: Helps only if the model actually records the failing test as the ticket. Otherwise it is tool bloat.

name: dsh-advisor
hypothesis: A second model passively reviews each turn and injects notes. Here the reviewer is also cheap unless configured otherwise.
whyForSweBench: A dumb reviewer on a dumb solver can still catch missed tests. Cost doubles.

name: dsh-code-intel
hypothesis: Tree-sitter symbol index plus lexical / embedding search.
whyForSweBench: Lite bugs are usually in one file, but finding the right symbol beats grep-thrash on Django.

name: dsh-plugin-knowledge-graph
hypothesis: CONTAINS / EXPORTS / IMPORTS graph over the checkout.
whyForSweBench: Helps when the failing test and the fix live in different modules. Can confuse a cheap model with graph jargon.

name: dsh-context-proxy
hypothesis: On-demand context_query / context_slice / context_grep over the session log instead of stuffing everything into the prompt.
whyForSweBench: Cheap models drown in traces. Thin retrieval should help long pytest loops.

name: billion-context-dsh
hypothesis: Model-driven context compression — the model decides what to keep.
whyForSweBench: Flash models are bad compressors. This may drop the failing assertion. High variance.

name: dsh-context-doctor
hypothesis: Read-only audit of instruction chains, skill catalogs, and tool schemas.
whyForSweBench: Does not add solving skill. Useful as a meta-review input, not as a keep candidate for Lite.

name: dsh-tool-search
hypothesis: Hermes-style progressive disclosure: hide long-tail tools until searched.
whyForSweBench: Default DSH already has many tools. Slimming schemas should help a cheap model stay on bash + editor.

name: dsh-skillport
hypothesis: Progressive-disclosure index over Claude/Codex/Cursor skill libraries.
whyForSweBench: A short SWE-bench skill (repro → localize → patch → test) is high leverage. A huge skill dump is poison.

name: dsh-mneme
hypothesis: SQLite + Markdown memory with offline semantic search and dream consolidation.
whyForSweBench: Single-issue evals barely use long-term memory. May help within a 3-repeat campaign if it stores repo-specific facts.

name: dsh-mnemon
hypothesis: Three-tier Mnemon memory: runtime, documents, memory spaces.
whyForSweBench: Same caveat as other memory plugins. Prefer after a verification plugin is already kept.

name: distill
hypothesis: Background subagent reflection that writes reusable skills from the session.
whyForSweBench: If it extracts 'always run the fail-to-pass test first', keep. If it writes vague skills, drop.

name: dsh-memento
hypothesis: Bounded, approval-gated, auditable ctx.memory with snapshot injection.
whyForSweBench: Approval gates in headless eval will stall unless auto-approved. Treat as high-risk for unattended runs.

name: dsh-file-memory
hypothesis: Memorize key premises into a session notes file so compaction cannot drop them.
whyForSweBench: Cheap and likely useful: 'failing test is X, root cause is Y' should survive long traces.

name: dsh-premise-guard
hypothesis: Injects a one-shot notice when compaction drops a critical literal anchor.
whyForSweBench: Pairs with file-memory. Low cost, should almost never hurt.

name: dsh-memory
hypothesis: remember / recall / forget tools with per-turn prompt injection.
whyForSweBench: Per-turn injection can steal context from the issue. Test after file-memory, not before.

name: dsh-memory (cited)
hypothesis: Distilled facts carry session citations back to the lossless log.
whyForSweBench: More honest memory than free-form notes. Still secondary for Lite.

name: dsh-memory-meow
hypothesis: Project-scoped PROJECT.md snapshot plus auto-reflection after ReAct tasks.
whyForSweBench: A generated PROJECT.md per repo could help the 3 repeats share localization.

name: dsh-memory-evolve
hypothesis: Git-branch-aware long-term memory and background skill evolution.
whyForSweBench: Branch awareness is cute; evolution mid-eval is a reproducibility risk.

name: nowledge-mem-deepseek-harness
hypothesis: Context Bundle injection and turn-end thread capture across tools.
whyForSweBench: Cross-tool memory is out of scope for a disposable SWE-bench workspace.

name: dsh-subagent-tools
hypothesis: Per-call model / persona / toolFilter overrides for subagents.
whyForSweBench: Could let the cheap parent keep a slightly smarter localizer. Or explode cost.

name: dsh-preset-flash-director
hypothesis: Token-economical director that delegates deep reasoning to expert subagents.
whyForSweBench: If experts are also flash, this is just more hops. If a smart model is wired in, it breaks the cheap-eval contract.

name: mstar-harness
hypothesis: Skill-driven workflow agent for structured harness-loop engineering.
whyForSweBench: Heavy orchestration on a 300-instance cheap loop is likely overhead.

name: dsh_workflow
hypothesis: Generatable, resumable multi-agent workflow layer.
whyForSweBench: Same overhead concern. Queue it after simpler gates prove useful.

name: dsh-deep-research
hypothesis: Adaptive deep-research orchestrator on the official workflow engine.
whyForSweBench: Lite instances are self-contained. Web research usually hurts (wrong docs, wasted turns).

name: modsearch
hypothesis: Web / X search bridge returning structured JSON evidence.
whyForSweBench: Official issues sometimes need library docs. More often the model googles instead of reading the repo.

name: dsh-toolkit
hypothesis: Ten deterministic tools: json, regex, diff, stat, schema, …
whyForSweBench: A structured diff/json tool can help. Ten new schemas can also drown flash.

name: dsh-docker
hypothesis: Typed docker/compose control for the agent.
whyForSweBench: Official scoring already wraps Docker. Giving the solver docker is usually unnecessary and dangerous.

name: dsh-prompt-studio
hypothesis: Edit built-in system-prompt sections with live preview.
whyForSweBench: The plugin itself is an editor. The value is the prompt we write with it — captured as remixes below.

name: dsh-prompt-profile
hypothesis: Reusable Markdown prompt profiles with argument substitution.
whyForSweBench: A SWE-bench profile (repro, localize, smallest patch, run tests) is a strong cheap-model prior.

name: dsh-turn-rewind
hypothesis: Rewind conversation and workspace via a change ledger.
whyForSweBench: Lets the agent undo a bad edit instead of piling on. High potential.

name: dsh-sidechain
hypothesis: Persistent /side sessions and one-shot /btw forks.
whyForSweBench: A localization side-quest that cannot dirty the main tree is attractive.

name: forkprobe
hypothesis: Compare multiple skills on the same task and pick the winner.
whyForSweBench: Expensive (multiplies runs). Powerful if we only fork on hard instances.

name: dsh-continual-evolve
hypothesis: Versioned, rollback-safe evolution of prompts, memory, and skills from trajectories.
whyForSweBench: This is the closest community plugin to our outer loop. Risky to nest evolution inside a scored run.

name: dsh-evolve
hypothesis: The agent hot-mounts its own plugins mid-session.
whyForSweBench: Reproducibility nightmare for a benchmark. Almost certainly drop.

name: dsh-auto-continue
hypothesis: Auto-resume interrupted turns after timeouts or host crashes.
whyForSweBench: Does not add intelligence, but reduces wasted eval budget. Weak keep.

name: dsh-knowledge
hypothesis: Shared Markdown knowledge base with kb_add / kb_search.
whyForSweBench: A run-level KB of 'django 3.2 queryset gotchas' could transfer across the 50 instances.

name: llm-adaptive
hypothesis: Per-request complexity routing across providers.
whyForSweBench: Breaks the cheap-model contract unless every route is the eval model. Queue last.

name: remix: test-first gate
hypothesis: Local remix: inject a SWE-bench checklist and a `run_repro_tests` tool before any file edit.
whyForSweBench: Directly encodes the scoring function into the cheap model's working memory.

name: remix: plan before edit
hypothesis: Refuse the first workspace write until the agent writes a 5-line localization note.
whyForSweBench: Cheap models edit README. A hard gate is ruder and more effective than advice.

name: remix: failure notebook
hypothesis: Slimmer fail-logger: append-only FAILURES.md, injected each turn, no extra skill taxonomy.
whyForSweBench: Less schema than dsh-fail-logger. Better for flash if the community plugin is heavy.

name: remix: verify loop
hypothesis: Remix of dsh-proof + dsh-doublecheck: one `close_turn` tool that requires a passing local test command.
whyForSweBench: Combines two keep-candidates into a single cheaper seam.

name: remix: compact then act
hypothesis: After 8 tool calls, force a 10-line state card (failing test, files, next action) and drop raw logs.
whyForSweBench: Hand-rolled compression that keeps the assertion text. Safer than billion-context.

name: remix: mneme SWE notes
hypothesis: If mneme is kept, pin a schema: repo, failing test, root-cause file, patch hunk, outcome.
whyForSweBench: Turns generic memory into a SWE-bench transfer format across the 50 instances.

name: remix: longer bash timeout
hypothesis: Patch the default bash plugin timeout from 300s to 900s for Django test suites.
whyForSweBench: Not intelligence — infra. Still moves the score if the cheap model was killed mid-pytest.

name: remix: smallest-patch prior
hypothesis: System-prompt prior: edit one file, three hunks max, no drive-by refactors. Matches how Lite was filtered.
whyForSweBench: Lite gold patches are small by construction. Teaching that to flash should lift precision.

name: remix: disable web tools
hypothesis: Ablation: unload web search / browser plugins for the eval profile.
whyForSweBench: Default DSH web tools tempt the model off-repo. This remix measures that tax.

name: dsh-mcp-bridge
hypothesis: Wires MCP servers (GitHub, filesystem, memory, Playwright) into the agent as native tools.
whyForSweBench: Lite sandboxes have no Slack or Notion. Extra MCP schemas usually steal turns from pytest.
notes: User batch. Needs outbound MCP + tokens the eval machine will not have.

name: dsh-asc (context-compactor)
hypothesis: Model-driven surface compaction: the agent replaces old ranges with durable checkpoints instead of dropping them.
whyForSweBench: Flash loops drown in pytest traces. Compaction should help if the checkpoint keeps the failing test.
notes: No plugin named dsh-context-compactor. Mapped to lmst2/dsh-asc.

name: dsh-rag-kb (workspace-rag)
hypothesis: Local vector index over workspace files so the agent can pull cross-file symbols without naming them.
whyForSweBench: Helps Django-sized checkouts. Hurts if indexing burns the cheap model's first minutes.
notes: No plugin named dsh-workspace-rag. Mapped to AlowEnsoul/dsh-rag-kb.

name: dsh-plans (plan-and-solve)
hypothesis: Write a Markdown plan and verifier checklist before any source edit, then execute against that checklist.
whyForSweBench: Lite tasks are short. A plan helps if it stays under a page; ceremony burns the cheap context window.
notes: No plugin named dsh-plan-and-solve. Mapped to Optim-Agent/dsh-plans.

name: dsh-tool-validator
hypothesis: Catch malformed or repeated tool calls and force a one-argument change before retry.
whyForSweBench: Flash repeats the same broken pytest. A validator is cheap intelligence.
notes: No public plugin under this name. Local remix of the Cordis interceptor idea.

name: dsh-multi-agent-debate
hypothesis: Two competing localizations, same cheap model, pick one before the first edit.
whyForSweBench: A second provider would break the cheap-eval contract. Same-model debate still costs a turn.
notes: No public debate plugin. Local remix — both sides stay on the eval model.

name: dsh-subagent-claude-code-wrapper
hypothesis: Delegate execution to a Claude Code CLI while DeepSeek plans.
whyForSweBench: Uses Claude. Live scoring skips it so the cheap-model pin stays intact.

name: dsh-model-router
hypothesis: Route simple steps to flash and escalate hard ones to a smarter model.
whyForSweBench: Escalating to V4-Pro is exactly the cheap-eval leak. Live scoring skips it.
